source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 17. Exercises reused from the lesson; du'aas flagged for review. The surahs themselves are recited with Dr. Hassan; this lesson teaches their meanings.
topic: Meanings of Al-Masad, Al-Fil, Quraysh, Al-Ma'un, An-Nasr and Al-Kafirun

learn.en: Al-Masad (111): Abu Lahab and his wife hurt the Prophet ﷺ. Being related to good people doesn't save us — only our own faith and deeds.
learn.title: Al-Masad

learn.en: Al-Fil (105): Abraha came with elephants to destroy the Ka'bah; Allah sent birds with stones of baked clay. No one can defeat Allah's plan.
learn.title: Al-Fil

learn.en: Quraysh (106): Allah made their winter and summer journeys safe and gave them food and safety. We thank Him by worshipping Him alone.
learn.title: Quraysh

learn.en: Al-Ma'un (107): be kind to orphans and the poor, pray on time for Allah — not to show off — and lend small things to neighbours.
learn.title: Al-Ma'un

learn.en: An-Nasr (110): after Allah's help and victory, people entered Islam in crowds. When we succeed, we praise Allah and ask His forgiveness.
learn.title: An-Nasr

learn.en: Al-Kafirun (109): a Muslim worships Allah alone and never mixes it with anything else. “For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.”
learn.title: Al-Kafirun

quiz.en: Which surah tells of birds with stones of baked clay?
Which surah teaches kindness to orphans and lending to neighbours?
Which surah ends: “For you is your religion, and for me is my religion”?
Which surah tells of safe winter and summer journeys?
True or false? Being related to good people is enough to save us.

think.q: Which of these six surahs do you know by heart? Which one will you learn next?
think.a: Revise one with your teacher every day — a little each day!

parents.summary: Meanings of six short surahs: Al-Masad, Al-Fil, Quraysh, Al-Ma'un, An-Nasr, Al-Kafirun. The recitation is learnt with Dr. Hassan.
parents.tip: Ask him to explain one surah's meaning to you in his own words.
